summary.title: Salary Negotiation: Make More Money, Be More Valued
summary.one_liner: Learn why salary negotiation matters so much for engineers, how employers actually view hiring costs, and why you should never name a number first.
takeaways: Salary negotiation has an outsized, compounding effect on lifetime earnings, so even a few minutes of better negotiating can be worth a lot.
Employers see employees in fully-loaded cost terms (often 150-200% of salary), so small salary asks are usually minor to them.
Only negotiate after reaching a 'Yes-If' agreement in principle with someone who has hiring authority, and always negotiate offers.
Avoid giving a number first; deflect requests for salary history or expectations by refocusing on mutual fit.
summary.summary: This long essay by Patrick McKenzie argues that engineers are poor at salary negotiation and explains why it matters: small raises compound over years and employers have far more budget flexibility than employees assume. It covers the employer's view of fully-loaded costs, the hiring manager's incentives, and how the hiring process should be structured so negotiation starts only after a Yes-If agreement. The page is written as an opinionated, anecdote-driven guide rather than a formal tutorial, and it ends with scripted responses to common objections such as 'I need a number to move the process forward.'
